headline: Brent down 6% is the first real crack in the inflation trade 48 hours before the Fed — but the unwind has gone offshore, with Korea at -22.8% on the month and a -3.1 sigma print.
summary: The oil tax is finally being refunded, and it started at the seaborne end. Brent fell 6.0% to 109.76 while WTI only gave back 2.2% to 100.95; RBOB dropped another 3.3% and is now -8.5% on the month at z=-0.90. Oil/gold is -2.7% today, though still +17.2% on the month and sitting in the 95th percentile. That matters because crude has been the sole engine behind a rates composite of -44 and an inflation composite of -47. The curve is already telling you the tightening impulse is decelerating even as levels stay ugly: 10s at exactly 5.00%, 2s 4.69%, 5s 4.82%, but acceleration z-scores of -2.12 on the 2-year, -1.98 on the 5-year and -1.47 on the 10-year, with 2s and 5s down 16bp and 17bp on the month. MOVE fell 3.3% to 103.31. The offsets are real and they are domestic: natural gas ripped 14.5% in one session to 3.023, 5-year breakevens sit at 2.48% (+14bp on the month, z=0.61) against 10-year breakevens of 2.34%, and the 30-year mortgage is pinned at 7.32%, the 94th percentile. The FOMC decides Wednesday into that mix.

What changed versus Friday is the geography of the pain. Friday it was the crowded defensive hideouts that paid, with XLP -1.9% and semis finally leading. Today the damage is offshore and concentrated: KOSPI -1.5% to 5,469, now -22.8% on the month at z=-3.14 with acceleration -2.76 — the single worst reading anywhere on the board — and EWY -18.5% on the month at z=-2.22. Nikkei -0.8% and -6.3% on the month. Europe is the mirror image: DAX +0.8%, CAC +0.7%, FTSE +0.5%, Euro Stoxx +0.4%. Crucially USD/KRW is actually *falling*, -3.1% on the month and in the 0.4 percentile, so this is a domestic memory/AI equity unwind, not capital flight. The same unwind runs through US internals: SMH -12.3% and SOXX -15.5% on the month, MU -18.1%, AMD -15.9% with acceleration -2.05, QQQ/SPY acceleration -2.29, and META -9.4% on the week with an acceleration z of -2.97 going into hyperscaler earnings.

But call it what it is — rotation, not liquidation. RSP/SPY has an acceleration z-score of +3.03, the highest number in the entire digest, with a 1-month z of 1.84 and +3.5% on the month; equal-weight is +2.5% over a month in which the S&P is -1.1% and the Nasdaq 100 is -5.0%. Software over semis is the cleanest expression: IGV/SMH +16.7% on the month and +33.8% on the quarter, z=2.42 with acceleration 1.92, and still only the 39th percentile of its own year. CIBR added 7.4% on the week, MSFT is +4.8% on the month, PLTR +60.1% on the quarter. Copper held at 6.5125 (+0.6%), copper/gold is at the 100th percentile and DBC at the 100th percentile — the cycle pulse is not endorsing a recession.

Where it stays dangerous is price of risk, not price of growth. VIX is 19.72, +32.6% on the month at z=1.26 with acceleration 0.88, VIX/VIX3M at 0.9497 (z=1.49, acceleration 1.05) and SKEW at 151.8 — the term structure is flattening into the Fed. Credit is quietly worse again: HYG/IEF is -2.2% on the month at z=-1.63 with acceleration -1.32, HYG sits in the 36th percentile while the S&P sits in the 87th, and BKLN is at z=-1.06. High-beta/low-vol is -15.4% on the month at z=-2.46 with acceleration -2.76 and growth/value is at the 4th percentile of its year — the index is near highs while everything inside it de-risks. The hedges are not helping: gold is 4,028 (+0.5% today but -6.8% on the month, 5th percentile) and gold/silver is +10.9% on the month. EM remains split down the middle — Brazil is a bull market (EWZ +14.0% on the month, BVSP z=1.73, USDBRL -1.1% today to 4.9931 at the 13th percentile) while Mexico is a currency accident in progress (USDMXN z=3.02, +8.3% on the month, 100th percentile, acceleration 1.46).

good.text: Crude finally cracked from the seaborne end: Brent -6.0% to 109.76, WTI -2.2% to 100.95, gasoline -3.3% today and -8.5% on the month at z=-0.90. The single biggest input to the -47 inflation composite just reversed.
The rate-rise impulse is decelerating even with 10s at 5.00%: acceleration z of -2.12 on 2s, -1.98 on 5s, -1.47 on 10s, with 2s -16bp and 5s -17bp on the month and MOVE down 3.3% to 103.31.
Breadth is broadening violently under a flat index: RSP/SPY acceleration z of +3.03 (highest on the board), 1m z=1.84, equal-weight +2.5% on the month against SPX -1.1%.
Software is eating semis, not dying with them: IGV/SMH +16.7% on the month at z=2.42 with acceleration 1.92, CIBR +7.4% on the week, IGV +6.0%, MSFT +4.8% on the month.
No recession confirmation from the cycle metals: copper 6.5125 (+0.6%), copper/gold at the 100th percentile and +4.3% on the month, DBC also at the 100th percentile.
Brazil keeps compounding: EWZ +14.0% on the month (z=1.59), BVSP z=1.73 with +10.4%, and USDBRL -1.1% today to 4.9931, the 13th percentile of its year.

bad.text: Korea is a -3.1 sigma event: KOSPI -1.5% today, -22.8% on the month at z=-3.14 with acceleration -2.76; EWY -18.5% on the month at z=-2.22; MU -18.1% and SOXX -15.5% on the month. Faster, not stabilising.

Internal de-risking is accelerating while the index holds: high-beta/low-vol -15.4% on the month at z=-2.46 with acceleration -2.76, growth/value at the 4th percentile, MTUM z=-1.74, QQQ/SPY acceleration -2.29.
Vol is bid into Wednesday's FOMC: VIX 19.72 (+32.6% on the month, z=1.26, acceleration 0.88), VIX/VIX3M at 0.9497 with z=1.49, SKEW 151.8.
Credit keeps diverging from equities: HYG/IEF -2.2% on the month at z=-1.63 with acceleration -1.32, HYG in the 36th percentile versus the S&P in the 87th, BKLN z=-1.06.

The household cost channel is still tightening despite cheaper crude: natural gas +14.5% in a single session, 5-year breakevens 2.48% (+14bp on the month), 30-year mortgage 7.32% at the 94th percentile.
The peso is breaking: USDMXN at z=3.02, +8.3% on the month, 100th percentile with acceleration 1.46 — and the dollar-based Mexico ETF is only +2.5% on the month against +8.7% for the local index.

trades.name: Belly duration via IEF
trades.line: Long IEF: Brent -6% gives the curve its first excuse
trades.expr: Buy IEF outright, or 5-year note futures (FVZ6); size to ~1.5x normal because the 2-year is doing the work. Overlay: sell 10y 5.25% strike risk via a payer spread if you want carry.
trades.thesis: Crude has been the only thing driving the rates composite to -44. Brent -6.0% and gasoline -8.5% on the month at z=-0.90 remove the marginal inflation bid just as the curve's upward acceleration collapses.
trades.trigger: Acceleration z-scores of -2.12 (2y), -1.98 (5y), -1.47 (10y) with 2s already -16bp and 5s -17bp on the month, MOVE -3.3% to 103.31, and Brent down 6% in a session two days before the FOMC.
trades.stop: 10-year back above 5.15%, or 5-year breakevens through 2.60% (from 2.48%), or a hawkish Oct 28 statement that re-prices December.

trades.name: Short HYG / long LQD
trades.line: Short junk vs IG: HYG 36th pctile, SPX 87th
trades.expr: Short HYG, long LQD dollar-for-dollar (duration-light credit-quality pair). Alternative: buy HYG Dec 76 puts.
trades.thesis: The AI capex-debt story is leaking into high yield before it shows in equities. HYG/IEF is -2.2% on the month at z=-1.63 with acceleration -1.32 while the S&P sits at the 87th percentile of its range — that gap closes down, not up.
trades.trigger: HYG at the 36th percentile with BKLN at z=-1.06, against VIX +32.6% on the month and the VIX term structure at 0.9497 (z=1.49). Credit is confirming the vol bid, equities are not.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF reclaims 0.862 (back to flat on the month) or HYG closes above 78.0.
trades.target: HYG/IEF to 0.825; 250-300bp of outperformance on the pair.

trades.name: Long IGV / short SMH
trades.line: Software over semis: IGV/SMH z=2.42, still 39th pctile
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH, equal notional. Express the tail with SMH Dec puts against long IGV stock.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is being re-sorted, not abandoned: capital is leaving the memory/hardware leg and funding software and security. The ratio has moved 33.8% in a quarter yet still sits in the 39th percentile of its own 52-week range, so this is early in a mean reversion, not late in a momentum chase.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH z=2.42 with acceleration 1.92; IGV +6.0% and CIBR +7.4% on the week while SOXX -3.1% and SMH -12.3% on the month; the Korea leg of the same trade is at a -3.14 sigma (KOSPI -22.8%) with MU -18.1% and AMD -15.9%.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below 0.195 (gives up half the monthly move), or SMH/SPY reclaiming its 200-day with two consecutive >1% relative days.

trades.name: Long RSP / short QQQ
trades.expr: Long RSP, short QQQ, equal notional, rebalanced weekly. Put it on before Wednesday's hyperscaler prints.
trades.thesis: The index is holding while leadership rotates out of the megacap AI complex into everything else. Equal-weight is +2.5% on the month against NDX -5.0%; that is a durable regime change in internals, and it is the cheapest way to stay long equities without owning the earnings risk.
trades.trigger: RSP/SPY acceleration z of +3.03 and 1m z of 1.84 — the strongest acceleration in the digest — against QQQ/SPY acceleration -2.29 and META at acceleration -2.97 after -9.4% on the week, straight into big-tech results.
trades.stop: RSP/SPY back below 0.2805, or two consecutive sessions where QQQ outperforms SPY by more than 1%.

trades.name: Long EWZ / short EWW
trades.line: LatAm split: BRL at 13th pctile, MXN at 100th
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, equal notional. Pure relative FX-plus-equity expression; no index hedge needed.
trades.thesis: EM has bifurcated and the currencies are telling you which half to own. Brazil has falling FX and rising equities; Mexico has a currency at a 3-sigma blow-out while the local index rallies — dollar investors in Mexico are already paying for it.
trades.trigger: USDBRL -1.1% today to 4.9931 (-3.8% on the month, 13th percentile) with EWZ +14.0% on the month at z=1.59 and BVSP z=1.73; versus USDMXN at z=3.02, +8.3% on the month, 100th percentile with acceleration 1.46, while EWW managed only +2.5% on the month against MXX's +8.7%.
trades.stop: USDBRL back above 5.25, or USDMXN reversing below 17.8 (peso stress resolved).
trades.target: 12-15% on the pair over the horizon.

trades.name: Health care via XLV
trades.line: Long XLV: +7.3% rel on the month, acceleration 1.66
trades.expr: Buy XLV; overweight the barbell inside it with LLY and UNH. Finance by underweighting XLP, which is already at z=1.80 and broke on Friday.
trades.thesis: This is the only defensive group with actual earnings momentum rather than just a rate-duration bid. It works whether the Fed is hawkish or crude keeps falling, and it does not depend on the AI complex.
trades.trigger: XLV +6.2% on the month at z=1.39 with acceleration 1.66, relative strength +7.3% on the month and +7.4% on the quarter in the 95th percentile; LLY +10.6% and UNH +12.6% on the month; IHI acceleration 1.75.
trades.stop: XLV closes below 170 (through the 50-day and giving back half the monthly gain), or relative strength versus the S&P turns negative on a 1-month basis.

trades.name: Fade XOP
trades.expr: Short XOP, or buy Dec 190 puts. Keep it small and pair against long XLE if you want to stay structurally long energy and only short the beta leg.
trades.thesis: E&P is the most extended thing on the board on the exact day its driver broke. XOP is +61.8% year-to-date, at the 100th percentile of its range and 20.4% above its 200-day, priced for triple-digit crude that just lost 6% in Brent.
trades.trigger: Brent -6.0% to 109.76 and WTI -2.2% to 100.95, gasoline -3.3%, while OIH printed +5.4% and XOP +2.4% on Friday — the equity leg has not marked to the commodity yet. XLE relative strength is +12.3% on the month, a crowded, late-stage read.
trades.stop: Brent closes back above 118, or XOP makes a new high above 208.
